If you believe in karma and have ever been on the receiving end of an SFMTA ticket that was totally BS (so, basically every San Franciscan), think twice before giving this guy your business.

I’ve been a customer here twice. You’d think that would earn a little neighborly goodwill. Nope. The owner called SFMTA because my back bumper was barely in the red zone of a gated and locked driveway. Not blocking anything. Just… existing near his precious red paint. I parked overnight and was there in the morning to head out to work, but by 8:08 a.m., he had already gleefully called SFMTA. Ticket issued. Mission accomplished. $108 ticket issued.  I'm sure that made his day, like fresh puppy blood.

I’ve lived in this neighborhood for twenty years, and let me tell you — this guy treats calling SFMTA the way most people treat happy hour. He lives for it. If there’s a citation fairy, he’s her favorite pen pal.

So if you loathe SFMTA and their zero-tolerance tax on anyone who owns a car in SF — while the city seemingly enforces nothing on anyone else — DO NOT reward our neighborhood ogre someone who does this to former customers and neighbors. Get your tires at Costco or literally anywhere else.

I called here today looking for some help with an O ring that got stuck in my tire valve stem. As a result, I couldn’t fill air.

The gentleman I spoke with indicated that it was impossible to remove. But in truth, it was easy to remove with a pick tool, or in my case, curved eyebrow scissors. After removing the tool, I filled my tires fine.

He also quoted $75 for a valve stem replacement, which is nearly the cost of a new tire from some suppliers. $30 is closer to market.
This shop is expensive!

I came here in October. I called to see how long it would take. They told me approximately 1 hour (on a week day) which is reasonable, especially because I'm working too. They didn't ask me what the year, make and model of my car. Once I arrived (10 minutes later), I was told to come back at 4pm (6 hours later). I had to walk to work.

They were reasonable on the cost, though.

I came here wanting to like this shop, considering the high number of positive reviews.  I got bad news that all four of my tires were beyond repair (this is obviously not the shop's fault).  When I told the individual (I presume the owner) that my tires were recently replaced and should be under warranty, he kept telling me he couldn't give me a piece of paper saying the tires were looked at and they were beyond repair for "liability reasons."  I don't get it.  I understand the shop wants to sell tires and I was trying to make a warranty claim with tirerack, instead of buying immediately.  He also couldn't blow some air into my tire so I could drive away, for "liability reasons."  I've had better and friendlier service in numerous auto shops.  I did also think the $80 quote to do a flat repair (before we realized they were not repairable) was quite expensive compared to other shops in the city.
My go to shop for anything tires. Make your life easy. Skip the chain shops. Just go here.
